architecture.product: Windows NVDA synthesizer add-on exposing Google's bundled WASM TTS engine through an installed Chromium browser runtime, with user-managed voice packages.
runtime_flow: The global plugin registers settings, voice-manager UI, optional startup update checks and optional background browser-runtime standby preparation.
SynthDriver loads the bundled engine/catalog, filters installed usable voice packages, creates a WavePlayer and either claims a ready standby bridge or creates one.
NVDA speech sequences enter a worker queue. The driver segments text, resolves normal settings or automatic language profiles, handles indexes/prosody and uses a short in-memory PCM cache.
ChromeTtsBridge coordinates BrowserProcessManager, CdpClient and WasmTtsEngineBridge. A loopback HTTP server serves the harness, bundled engine and installed voice packages.
The selected Chrome/Edge/Brave runtime loads the harness. CDP Runtime.evaluate invokes synthesis; Runtime.bindingCalled returns base64 PCM audio and progress events.
Python validates PCM and feeds nvwave.WavePlayer. Cancellation and teardown must stop queued/current work and release or terminate browser/CDP resources.
Voice Manager explicitly downloads/imports/removes packages. The updater independently checks a stable manifest, validates downloaded size/SHA256 and delegates installation to NVDA.

components.responsibility: NVDA synth driver, worker queue, settings, language profiles, segmentation, indexes, silence shortening, PCM cache and player lifecycle
Loopback server and path handling, browser startup/fallback/profiles, CDP transport, WASM request/events, runtime recycle and cleanup
Optional background readiness, directory-change watchers, bridge handoff and cancellation
Engine/catalog inspection, language/speaker/package metadata, dependencies, package storage and size/SHA256 verification caches
Automatic language detection and architecture-specific Windows CLD2 DLL selection
Browser harness and bundled Google WASM engine; audio processing and session-token guarding
Settings, voice package operations and accessible read-only status controls
Stable update metadata, download verification, UI/controller state and release-manifest generation
Source-string extraction, translation checks, .mo compilation and localized manifest generation
Version/build metadata, syntax/conflict/voice-data checks and .nvda-addon ZIP packaging

declared_support.evidence_limit: These are repository declarations; this review did not run NVDA 2024.1 or 2026.1.
declared_support.platforms: Interactive speech runtime requires Windows and a supported installed Chrome, Edge or Brave browser.
declared_support.edge_runtime: Microsoft Edge WebView2 is required when Edge is the effective browser runtime; Chrome and Brave must not acquire this requirement.

review_coverage: Browser/CDP bridge and loopback file routing
contracts_to_preserve: Voice downloads are explicit Voice Manager actions; speech and preload must never download packages.
Expose only installed usable voices and preserve dependency relationships.
Long operations remain off the NVDA GUI thread; workers marshal UI changes through wx.CallAfter.
Cancellation must remain responsive and late audio must not enter another request or the cache.
Use focusable read-only controls with real label association for status/help text; localized strings must remain wrapped in the translation mechanism.
Background readiness remains off by default and disabled in secure mode.
Keep Chrome/Edge/Brave fallback, runtime-specific profiles, cancellation propagation and bridge ownership intact.
Retain size/SHA256 verification for packages/updates and the existing loopback path-safety/isolation controls.
Do not bundle .zvoice files, browser profiles or __pycache__ in the add-on.
The localized changelog must match the base manifest version; generated .mo and localized manifests come from source translations.
architecture.test_inventory: No automated interactive/runtime test suite was found. build.sh validates conflicts, Python/JavaScript syntax, source-tree voice-data exclusion and archive structure; build_i18n.py provides concrete localization validation. These checks do not establish NVDA speech or accessibility behavior.

missing_messages: &Keep Google TTS browser runtime ready in the background
Keep Google TTS browser runtime ready in the background
Off. Google TTS For NVDA will start the browser runtime only when you choose Google TTS as the current synthesizer.

invariants: Runtime behavior and the default-off background-readiness setting do not change.
zh_CN localized release information describes the same version and feature semantics as the base manifest.
The enabled-status text accurately states that background readiness may use additional memory and keep runtime files open until disabled or NVDA exits.
All translated placeholders remain equivalent to source placeholders; accelerators remain usable.
Generated .mo and localized manifest remain consistent with nvda.po.
Other locales, voice catalogs, languageSort.json, engine files and package/download behavior are unaffected.
No translated text promises that browser startup timing is completely fixed.
acceptance_criteria: The all-locale validator reports no zh_CN missing translation or obsolete source-string errors.
The localized manifest contains the 0.6 changelog rather than 0.5.5 release information.
On NVDA with a Simplified Chinese UI, the checkbox, group/status label and off/on messages are translated and understandable.
The checkbox retains a working accelerator and the status field remains keyboard focusable with its label read before the read-only edit role.
Settings preview still saves only through OK/Apply; Cancel does not persist a change.
Other four currently validated locales continue passing.
The final archive includes the regenerated zh_CN files and excludes __pycache__, .zvoice data and browser profiles.
regression_scenarios: Background readiness off, on while Google TTS is current, and on while another synth is current.
Settings OK/Apply versus Cancel with the runtime-ready checkbox changed.
Long translated status strings wrap and remain fully readable through keyboard review.
Translator placeholder/accelerator/multiline quoting mistakes are caught by checks or manual review.
Fresh installation versus updating an existing add-on: correct localized release information is visible in the resulting package.
No unrelated locale or normal speech setting changes in the diff.
risks: Editing generated .mo or manifest directly can appear to fix the archive while the next i18n build overwrites the repair.
A translation can pass structural checks yet misstate the memory/startup trade-off; native-language review is still needed.
Longer translated strings may expose Windows dialog layout issues that Linux syntax/build checks cannot detect.
A full i18n build may refresh a shared template or other generated outputs; keep the final diff restricted and inspect it.
findings.rollback: Revert the zh_CN source and its generated artifacts together if a translation/layout regression is found, rebuild the package and mark the localization defect OPEN again. Avoid reverting runtime code or changing version/support declarations as part of this translation rollback.
